sub_unit_name: Internal treatment of Boiler feed water - Calgon conditioning - Phosphate conditioning - Colloidal conditioning

content.title: Internal Treatment of Boiler Feed Water
content.description: Internal treatment involves adding suitable chemicals directly into the boiler water to prevent scale formation, sludge deposition, and corrosion. It is commonly used along with external water treatment methods.

content.content: Boiler feed water often contains dissolved salts that cause scale and sludge formation. Internal conditioning converts these salts into soft, non-adherent sludge or soluble complexes that can be removed by blow-down operations, thereby improving boiler efficiency and extending equipment life.

content.title: Need for Internal Treatment
content.content: Internal treatment minimizes scale formation, prevents corrosion, improves heat transfer, and reduces maintenance costs in boilers.

Calgon conditioning uses sodium hexametaphosphate (NaPO3)6, commonly called Calgon. It reacts with calcium ions to form soluble complex compounds, preventing the formation of hard scales inside the boiler.

content.title: Principle of Calgon Conditioning
content.description: Calgon forms stable soluble complexes with calcium and magnesium ions, thereby preventing their precipitation as scales.

content.content: In phosphate conditioning, chemicals such as trisodium phosphate (Na3PO4), disodium phosphate (Na2HPO4), or monosodium phosphate (NaH2PO4) are added to convert hardness-producing salts into soft phosphate sludge.

Colloidal conditioning uses organic substances such as kerosene, tannin, agar-agar, starch, or sodium alginate. These substances surround precipitated particles and keep them suspended in water, preventing their deposition on boiler surfaces.

items.question: Scale Prevention
items.answer: Prevents deposition of hard scales inside boilers.

items.question: Improved Heat Transfer
items.answer: Maintains efficient heat transfer and reduces fuel consumption.

items.question: Easy Maintenance
items.answer: Soft sludge can be removed easily through blow-down.

items.question: Longer Boiler Life
items.answer: Reduces corrosion and increases the service life of boiler equipment.

content.title: Industrial Importance
content.content: Internal conditioning is widely used in thermal power plants, chemical industries, textile mills, sugar factories, and paper industries to maintain efficient boiler operation.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Internal treatment uses chemicals added directly into boiler water.
Calgon conditioning forms soluble complexes with hardness ions.
Phosphate conditioning converts hardness salts into soft phosphate sludge.
Colloidal conditioning keeps precipitates suspended and prevents deposition.
Blow-down removes the sludge formed during conditioning.
